Elon Musk Says Crash Wouldn’t Happen If Autopilot Was Used
In a series of posts on
X

on Wednesday, the billionaire responded to a now-deleted ABC News post, accusing the outlet of “misleading the public” about the details of the crash. The crash, which ABC News reported took place at 2:43 a.m. on Wednesday in Manhattan, occurred after a Tesla Model Y crashed into scaffolding.
Why are you misleading the public?
The car was being driven by 27-year-old
Alejandra Paharsingh
, who was traveling with her friend, 27-year-old
Elise Suomi
, who died in the crash.

Paharsingh was injured and taken to the hospital. According to a report by ABC’s New York station, she has been arrested by law enforcement on charges of vehicular manslaughter, leaving the scene of an accident resulting in death and driving while impaired.
Musk, in response to user
Reddit Lies

on X, denied the involvement of Tesla’s driver assistance technology in the incident. “It wasn’t the car,” the CEO said. He added that if “Autopilot was in use, they [the vehicle] would not have crashed.”

“The legacy media will never forgive Tesla for failing to advertise with them,” the Tesla CEO said in the post, but did not provide any further details.
The legacy media will never forgive Tesla for failing to advertise with them
Elon Musk Touts Cybercab
Musk has touted the company’s Cybercab as the beginning of a “golden era” in transportation, saying that the vehicle without a steering wheel and pedals was gold in color to reflect that very change.

However, questions remain about the efficacy of Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) system, as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) opened a probe into the cab’s deployment in Austin.
